no_action.rule_1_annotations: 0 rows. No slash forms, brackets, parentheticals or glosses in any target_text across all 493 drafts. (Two speaker LABELS carry a time-of-day parenthetical — 'Neighbour (10:30 pm)' in dan and isl, and 'Barista (3 pm)' in isl — these are the speaker column, not learner-facing line text, and were left alone.)
no_action.rule_3_register: 0 rows in all four languages. Danish and Norwegian polite 'De/Dem/Deres' and Swedish polite 'Ni/Er' do not occur anywhere in the drafts; every second-person form is du/dere/ni-plural/I-plural, which is correct modern usage in service and stranger scenes alike after the Scandinavian du-reform. Icelandic has no living V form; every occurrence of 'þér' in the isl drafts is the dative singular of informal 'þú' (e.g. 'Hvað má bjóða þér?'), not the archaic polite nominative. No 'yður/yðar' anywhere. Tom's exception clause for service scenes therefore has nothing to bite on in Nordic — this is a real linguistic fact, not an omission.
